description: `config migrate` is Rust-only (no Python oracle leaf to parity-check against), so this scenario pins Rust's own contract directly, parsing the config with plain `toml_edit` rather than the full loader (which would itself refuse a retired role name inside `roles_allowed`, card finding `a_retired_role_key_in_roles_allowed_is_also_refused_naming_the_migrator`). A retired role name inside an account's `roles_allowed` array (a VALUE, not a key — `[roles.<name>]` table headers are rewritten by conformance's own `role_translate.translate_config_toml` before this ever reaches Rust, so this is the one retired-spelling position that still reaches the binary unmodified) is enough to trigger a migration: `--dry-run` renders a unified-style diff and writes nothing; the same command with neither `--dry-run` nor `--backup` refuses outright rather than silently doing nothing or silently writing.

home.config_toml:
[projects.sandbox]
path = "{{PROJECT:sandbox}}"

[accounts.explorer-seat]
kind = "codex"
config_dir_var = "CODEX_HOME"
config_dir = "{{HOME}}"
pool = "codex:test"
roles_allowed = ["fixer"]

expect.stderr: config migrate requires --backup to write changes; use --dry-run to preview
